## Recursive rule and proof test {#ss3-definition .ap-lesson .ap-proof}

For first term $a$ and common difference $d$, the **recursive rule** is

$$a_1=a,\qquad a_n=a_{n-1}+d\quad(n\ge2).$$

::: {.ap-proof-step .fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
<h3>Proving a sequence is arithmetic</h3>

Show that the difference is the same constant for **every term after the first**:

$$a_n-a_{n-1}=d\qquad\text{for every }n\ge2\text{ in the sequence}.$$

:::

::: {.ap-proof-step .fragment data-fragment-index="1"}
<h3>For three terms</h3>

$$a_3-a_2=a_2-a_1$$

The two consecutive differences must be equal.

:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 11 · Recursive rule and proof</p>

::: notes

Initially show only the recursive rule and its starting value. The same constant d applies at every step. First click introduces the proof test. Use later term minus earlier term consistently. For a finite sequence, test every index from 2 up to its final index. For an infinite sequence, establish the equality for arbitrary n≥2.

Second click specialises the test to a sequence of exactly three terms: a_3−a_2=a_2−a_1. Checking this equality for the first three terms of a longer sequence establishes only that those three terms are in AP. The remaining differences must also be constant. Proceed immediately to Example 3.2.

:::
